BLACKWATER '89 5. The Marconi Sailing Club have been trying to win the Colwyn Stone Challenge Trophy since it was first awarded in 1981, However each year Rochester have managed to win by a mixture of good luck and good sailing. On Saturday 24 June 1989, the luck finally ran out. On a warm sunny day the combination of a fickle wind, a strong tide and a well sailed single-handed Mirror finally managed to do what world champions, fast boats and national level sailors had failed to do: Damian Boreham won the Colwyn Stone Trophy for MSC, It was like John Bertrand winning the America's Cup for Australia. The MSC team was: Ron Greygoose in a Solo, John Weedon in a Laser, Mike and Maggie Boreham in a 420, and their son Damian in a_ single-handed Mirror, The Rochester team was: Richard and Sharon Stone in a Wayfarer, Christopher and Alexander Jibb in a Mirror, and Peter and Gordon Belcher in Lasers, On paper it was a strong team - Richard hed won the trophy four times; Peter had won it three times; Gordon had sailed in the event for fourteen years; whilst Christopher showed great promise last year. The wind was light and from the West, the tide was coming in from the East. The Rochester team made @ good start and on the second leg were in first, second and third places. However the wind stayed light and as the fleet ran downwind against the tide, the single-handed Mirror was too close for comfort; Damian sonehow managed to control three sails and kept close to the fleet, staying out of the tide, to win. Rochester packed well with Peter Belcher second - first on the water but just eight seconds behind on handicap. Richard Stone was third, Gordon Belcher fifth and Christopher Jibb sixth, At lunch Rochester were 4? points ahead and ready for the sea breeze to cane in and blow the single-handed Mirror's chances, rm, was not to be - the wind for the second race was even more fickle, After a long beat with the tide the fleet had to run against it along the island shore; John Weedon, now in a Kestrel crewed by Lucy Boreham, pulled away and appeared to have an unassailable lead, Peter Belcher and Richard Stone were chasing him hard and Gordon Belcher was trying to keep Ron Greygoose under control. Damian Boreham was out in the tide and appeared to have blown his chances. Once again the final run against the tide changed everything. The boats at the front of the fleet sailed into a hole with Peter Belcher and Richard Stone overtaking John Weedon; then the wind changed direction to the East and freshened as, belatedly, the sea breeze came in, Peter and Richard were first and second over the line, but the slower boats were now sailing in a good breeze and easily beat their handicap, Damian won the race, with Ron Greygoose second (despite almost capsizing at the last mark). Rochester's placings were three, four, five and eight with MSC placings one, two, six, seven, thus MSC won the second race by 4% points, Overall Damian Boreham won the Colwyn Stone Challenge Trophy with two firsts, whilst Rochester retained the Medway Cup for the team event, Again a very pleasant visit with good interesting sailing, good company and good food. -- The results of the 'HELMSMAN OF THE YEAR! Final for 1989 The winner of the 1989 'Helmsman of the Year' series :- MALCOLM GANDY Congratulations to Malcolm Gandy who won the Helmsman of the Year trophy after what must rank as one of the closest and most keenly contested H.o.Y finals for many a year. MalcoJm.saw an almost certain runaway victory suddenly turn into near defeat - only to snatch a well deserved but-hard-earned success in the last moments of the competion. Certainly, those of us who were able to watch the 1989 final witnessed a fine performance by all who took part, with victory and defeat being governed by the capricious activities of the wind and tide - aided and abetted (as always ) _ by the helms making the wrong decisions at the wrong time. Enough of poetry (poetry ? what poetry ?), let's get on with the report. Those taking part in the H.o.Y were :- Malcolm Gandy (Solo Fleet) Lee Tridini (Sailboard Fleet) Mike Duckmanton (Cat Fleet) Mike Hellewell (420 Fleet) Damian Boreham (Mirror Fleet) John Weedon (Handicap Fleet). All races were around 2 laps of the course D, A, E, No.1 and F marks, all passed to starboard with.a N-Nl! wind starting out at Force 4 - 5, later dropping to Force 1-2 and then picking up again to Force 3-4. "E' mark was placed near Osea island and directly to windward of 'A' mark and I reckon Graham Baker, driver of the Jack B, made a good job in positioning it just about right. It certainly provided a choice of route on the windward leg between A and E which undoubtedly proved crucial to the outcome of the Elimination Rounds. The formula for 1989 was that the 6 finalists were divided into two groups of three, each to race an Elimination Round of 3 races in Mirrors (swopping the boats for each race). The winner of each group would then meet in the final as a Match Race sailed in lasers, the winner to be the first to score two wins. The Elimination Round (single-handed Mirrors) - the two groups were :- Group 1 - Malcolm Gandy, Mike Hellewell and Lee Tridini Group 2 - Mike Duckmanton, John Weedon and Damian Boreham For obvious reasons, Damian was not allowed to sail either of the Boreham-owned Mirrors (Bumble and Lars Tinn) and these boats were allocated to Group l. Malcolm, John, Lee and Damian had all had experience of sailing Mirrors and Mike Duckmanton took the wise precaution of getting some Mirror experience during the Jackpot on the previous Sunday. Just as well - a Mirror handles somewhat differently from a Dart 18 catamaran ! Mike Hellewell stepped into the Mirror for the first time but was well used to mono-hull sailing in his 420. He did wonder why the jib kept failing to tack, that is until he realised he didn't have his usual crew (Irene) to do it for him. Races 1 and 2 provided much sport for the spectators as near victory turned into even nearer defeat with each tack and gybe. Mike Duckmanton capsized in Race 2 and Mike Hellewell spoiled a brilliant start in race 1 by going back because he thought he was over the line. At the end of race 2, the Elimination Round was still wide open with:- (a) Lee Tridini needing a win the the 3rd race of Group 1 in order to beat Malcolm Gandy and (b) John and Damian needing to finish ahead of each other (but not necessarily win) in the 3rd race of Group 2. Race 3 was a fine race with much swopping of the lead and lesser places all the way around. The outcome of the Elimination Round was that Malcolm (Group 1 winner) and Damian (Group 2 winner) went forward to face each other in the Match Race Final. The Match Race final (single-handed lasers) - Damian won the start of Race 1 but was soon overhauled by Malcolm who went on to win by almost 2 minutes. Race 2 saw Malcolm in the lead from the start and soon well ahead at the finish of the lst lap. These races were really a procession and, to be honest, a bit of a bore after the thrills and interest of the Mirror racing. So confident were we in the rescue boat that Malcolm would win the 2nd race (and the H.o.Y) that we planned to pick up 'E' as soon as both had passed it . Then an apparent miracle happened - the wind started to drop and Damian started to catch up. Gradually, inexorably, Damian caught, matched and then overtook Malcolm to win the 2nd race by 30 seconds. One win each and all to play for on the last race. Malcolm lead the 3rd race initially but lost the lead on the broad reach and run legs. An incident at 'F' mark on the first lap saw Malcolm doing a 720 which enabled Damian to establish a handy lead. Now another miracle - the wind started to increase again and Malcolm gradually whittled away the lead until, as Damian rounded 'F' mark to start the beat for the finish line, Malcolm was not many yards behind. With 156 yards to go they were level and the previous victories and defeats now counted for nothing. Malcolm eased his way ahead and won the race, and Helmsman of the Year, by 8 seconds.
